reviews.comment: Assignments every week which weren't too hard, but the final exam was. Study and turn everything in on time!
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is so easy until the final

Prof Beathard is so kind and understanding. The class literally requires minimal effort, do the Packback assignments every few Sundays (I missed one and it TANKED my grade). There is a LinkedIn assignment, research essay, and final, but the grading is SUPER chill. The class is interesting as well

The concept of this class is fantastic-learn about the career paths as a NUTR/FSTC major and have respected companies/people come talk about it every week. However, Dr. Beathard makes this class much more work than it needs to be with assignments and memorizing random things about people that came to speak to us for the final. Seems excessive.

This class had way too much work for what it was meant to be, and Dr. Beathard basically never taught the class. There is a final at the end of the class over all the previous lectures that is 30% of your grade. Go to class and fill in the questions she sends out and you will be alright.

Dr. Beathard is strict, but she wants you to learn and no matter how busy she is, she always has time to meet with you. You have to go to class. There are a lot of in-class participation assignments. Grading is strict and she has a specific way she wants you to say things. Mandatory textbook. Don't miss more than 2 classes excused or unexcused.

This is actually the most brain dead class ever. Why do I have to memorize things about other companies I won't work at and about rando people I don't care about. This class actually makes me mad that I have to memorize every lecture for the final. This class is actually stupid so if u dont have to take it do something else

This class is horrible. You would think it'd be simple because it is a ONE HOUR credit but no. Tons of time consuming assignments. Weekly speakers who come, don't answer of all of your questions and then the professor expects you to have it all memorized for the exam. Ridiculous amount of memorization expected and very specific questions.

not too bad, class isn't that exciting, basically all external speakers. she is sticky about phones and you have like 3 unexcused absences before points are taken off. basically all the class is 1 paper and the final

Beathard is a quality educator, though she is not very involved in the class. She will take time out of her day to reach out when you are not doing well. You have a group project, Packback assignments, and a few lecture-based exams. DO NOT MISS A PACKBACK DEADLINE. It will dramatically stunt your grade. This class is not difficult.

Show up to class. Complete the packsack assignments ON TIME. There is one group project, with some bonus point opportunities. Overall, the class wasn't too bad. I just thought that tests were unnecessary because they were specific questions from the presentations. So take notes! Since, there aren't many assignments, make the most of them.

Not a huge fan of this class. Only guest speakers, weirdly specific test questions, and wants EVERYTHING turned in on paper. Had to make trips to the printers multiple times. Overall, not the worst class, but keep every paper she gives you because there will be a time that it is needed to be resubmitted. Gave me a headache more than anything.

Go to class and make sure to take notes (&fill out all the questions bc u will NEED it for the exams). There were only 2 exams, a group project, packback, and smaller other assignments. Make sure to do well on exams and group project to ensure a B at least! Very interesting and fun class!

She did not teach, only had guest speakers for the whole semester. Pay attention and don't skip because you'll have 2 exams that ask you really specific questions and you have to memorize random trivia from the guest presentations in order to do well. Packbacks, one major group project. Not impressed with her.

The professor doesn't do much for the class as guest speakers lecture instead. Exams cover content guest speakers present (questions are specific). She uses Packback for weekly assignments and assigns a group essay (group is assigned). Little guidance was provided for the essay. She didn't post presented powerpoints until the end of the semester.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: NUTR 210 and FSCT 210 are the same class and it is not great by any means. The class consists of a new guest speaker every day. Dr. Beathard does not teach for a single class. Two exams over nit-picky details on the guest speaker's presentation. Very few grades so everything counts heavily. Large group project, not hard but definitely stressful.

Dr. Beathard's class is organized and she is specific about the way she wants things on her assignments. There are guest speakers over different companies and careers you can pursue. Take notes on the handouts. There is one major group project that requires a decent amount of effort. She is a very sweet lady and cares about her student's success!

The professor does nothing, guest speakers present for the semester. Doesn't post the presentations, and speaker sheet questions left unanswered. Assigned a useless group project over writing a nutritional research essay that is completely unrelated to the class content of careers in nutrition. A bad group & hard grading will bring down your grade.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Beathard is a very kind and caring professor! The class mainly consisted of presentations about career opportunities in nutrition and food science. It was a very interesting and easy class; the tests are simple if you come to class and take thorough notes, and the group project is a bit tedious but manageable. I really enjoyed this class!

Dr. Beathard is a good prof who genuinely cares about her students. The class itself is very useless and is basically a series of presenters who come and tell you about professional opportunities available to you with your major. Tests are memorization of random things that you won't ever need to know again. One group project. Silly, but easy A.

Great introduction to Texas A&M Nutrition. Class was structured around guest speakers with questions for each lecture. One large group project that's easy to do if you get lucky with a good group. Grading is clear with 2 large tests, 6 Packback questions, and a few other assignments. Super accessible outside of class and a super kind professor!

The class & test are all based on various guest speakers in the FSTC & Nutrition community. 2 tests based on a hodgepodge of the speakers presentations, a long/hard group essay, 10 packback posts for grades. She takes roll, has it in canvas but it doesn't count towards the overall grade. Why have it in the gradebook then? Could of had an A.

One of my favorite professors at A&M. She teaches 304 in a flipped format, which was actually helpful for learning because in class we would do activities like case studies. There is a lot of material and assignments in this class but if you stay organized it's very straightforward. Despite her busy schedule, she always made time to meet with me.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class would be better online than in person. She requires attendance even if its flooding. Strict grader and can be unnecessarily harsh. Class should not be required and is generally a waste of money and time. Speakers were interesting but not very relevant to a foodsci major. Notes ask questions speakers don't cover and you're tested over it.

Two tests all semester, material straight from guest speaker notes (sometimes oddly specific and irrelevant). Lots of memorization. Group project lasting all semester, a little tedious. Really tough grader I would say. Honestly felt like a waste of energy trying to memorize half a sem of guest speakers. I found it hard to pay attention.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Only had guest speakers, felt like a waste of a class because i didn't learn anything useful for actual life or my major (NUTR).
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The whole class in guest speakers, show up and take notes with guided notes and read over before exams. Group project- not super fun but durable, plenty of time.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Quiz questions are often based on guest speakers but sometimes aren't discussed in lectures so they can be difficult. If you hate group projects, avoid her. She doesn't care if you did all the work. I put in the peer eval that I wrote 95% of our paper required and others got a higher grade than what I got even though they did almost nothing.

Has little to no sympathy. The last thing she is worried about is her students succeeding. Chooses rules 100% over the students future. I won't take her again and advise people to steer clear of her if you can.

Sweet and caring Professor!!! She is very insightful and knowledgable. Gives very great feedback too! Attend class, take notes, and you will definitely pass the quizzes! No exams, only quizzes and a few projects including one group project! Easy A class!

I love Mrs. Beathard. I can tell she really enjoys what she does. She is very easy to approach and she replies to emails fairly quickly. Her weekly quizzes are simple questions from the 2 lectures during the week but the questions are often very specific so you have to really master the content before taking the quizzes. Overall, great prof.!!

This class is amazing if you are considering a field in nutrition or food science! Guest speakers are brought in, and the lectures are always interesting! She also gives amazing lectures! You will use Packback in this class, but don't fret- it is not too difficult. Two exams and a group project that are not hard at all. She is amazing, TAKE HER!!!!

Professor Beathard really cares about her students and is passionate about nutrition. Every assignment gives clear directions so getting high grades should not be a problem if you put in a decent amount of effort. The group project is a little difficult trying to collaborate with others, but she gives extra credit opportunities.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Ms. Beathard rarely teaches in the class and when she does she goes through too quickly the presentation. However, the class is really easy A go to class, do the presentation page (same questions on the test), keep on track and try with your group project (semester-long). The grading of the class is overall pretty generous.

This is an extremely easy class. There are guest lecturers every class and grading is easy. There's one group project, lots of busywork, and discussion posts. Attendance is mandatory but it's fine since you have to get the notes anyway. Just show up and do your work, it's an easy A. Learned absolutely nothing about nutrition though.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Literally all you have to do is show up. Attendance is mandatory anyway so why not? Big group project and a couple individual projects. She gives fair and good deadlines though to keep you on top of your own work.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: There are guest lectures which is annoying. Also, attendance is not part of the grade, but if you don't come and sign your name on the piece of paper, you get an X on ecampus. She does none of the grading, but her TA, Daniel does & is way too hard! There is a semester group project which you can't pick your groups so it SUCKS! DO not take her!
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: We're basically listening to guest speakers every single time. About half of the guest speakers are talking about info I don't even care about the slightest bit, but I'm forced to waste 50mins of my time sitting there and taking notes because we'll have about 50 test questions about the speakers. Some speakers were useful, but others weren't.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great prof, a lot of work. don't skip. read outside of class and watch online lectures. answer questions.

I love Mrs. Beathard not only as a prof but as a person. Super approachable and helpful. As long as you go to class (which might end in getting some yummy snacks) and check your notes with the TA, you will end up with a high A. Super informative if your looking for a career that is nutrition related.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: A LOT Of busy work for this class, but I got 100s on all of them. Easy class, but if it's not required for your major I wouldn't take it just due to the amount of extra work.

Easy A if you keep up with the work. There are a lot of little homework assignments and things to turn in, but they're very simple. You take notes based on guest lectures and she takes 1 point off per missed class (after 2 unexcused absences). Only 2 tests which are based off  guest speakers. 1 group project which isn't too tough.

Dr. Beathard is a great professor. This is an easy class as long as you attend. Attendance is taken and it matters. One midterm & final... basically split up into first & second semester speakers . One group project, put in the work and get an A. Come to class and learn from various speakers as to what directions you can take in your field.

This class was super easy. If you go to class and answer the questions on the presentation pages you will be fine. Study hard for the tests because there are only two! One group project that is also easy.

The work required for this seminar class is more than necessary. I took notes based on the presentation pages she gives you for each speaker but that wasn't enough for the exams. The group project is easy and there a bunch of little homework assignments to help boost your grade but if you don't do well on either of the tests you're kind of screwed.

This class was super easy and just like AGLS. You listen to a different speaker everyday and fill out a presentation page. Attendance is required, and there is only a mid-term and a final (non-cumulative). Can be an interesting class; the speakers are based off of career paths you can take with NUTR or FSC. There is a group project, but it's a joke

Takes attendance, takes points off if you miss too many lectures. Exams are based on questions you need to fill out when speakers come to your class. Easy class as long as you study and do all of the assignments.

Her class was not what I expected. It was more like college 101. She only taught the class once. She had speakers come in every day to talk about things offered at A&M along with different companies/ professional people who spoke about what they did. It was good to know, and I took a lot from it, just not what I expected. Easy but don't under estim

Dr. Beathard is a very sweet lady, class is mandatory for Nutrition majors and is an easy A. She takes attendance, so go to class otherwise points are deducted. Hardest thing about the class is the group project because it's hard to find times to meet up. Overall, go to class and do the presentation pages and you'll get an A.
